basis: 2026_01_NE_SEA (sealed shadow forecast, T-31h, scored) and 2026_01_SF_LA (T-18m, scored), plus the 2026-09-13 sealed slate
standing_rule: No modeling item is promoted on two games. Every P1 requires multi-game prospective evidence, pre-registered, decided out of sample. The P0 items are correctness and infrastructure and need no predictive evidence at all.
ordering_rationale: P0 first because a system that can silently skip a game, or model only quarterbacks, or score only by hand, cannot generate the evidence every P1 item needs. Q4 in particular BLOCKS Q5, Q6 and Q7: without automatic scoring there is no path to the sample floors.

queue.title: Sealed forecasts must stay discoverable across namespaces
queue.why: The ledger could not see a sealed, scored, git-tracked NE@SEA forecast, so a review reported its absence as a fact and halved the apparent evidence base. This is worse than a missing forecast: it corrupts conclusions rather than numbers, and it silently recurs on every namespace change.
queue.work: Shipped: sealed_index discovers by CONTENT across live, shadow and product namespaces, with an append-only namespace list and a regression test. Remaining: point the prospective scoring row and the research export at it so scoring, not just discovery, spans namespaces.

queue.title: Injury report completeness must be visible and actionable
queue.why: Twelve of twelve Sunday games are QB-only because report_status is unfilled. This is the single largest coverage loss in the system and it was invisible until completeness was computed from distributions.
queue.work: Report per-club filing state on every slate run; request the missing reports through the networked agent; assert that an all-unfilled injuries capture is INCOMPLETE rather than PASS.
queue.evidence_required: None for visibility. A DEGRADED appearance mode is a modeling change and needs >=3 games scored both ways.

queue.title: Canonical player eligibility across every allocation layer
queue.why: The QB path ignored the official inactive list while the non-QB path honoured it. One eligibility fact must reach every allocator or the layers describe different games.
queue.work: Audit the remaining allocators -- rushing_a1, targets_carries, td_layer -- for the same missing argument, and add one shared eligibility assertion covering all of them rather than one per layer.

queue.title: Automatic authoritative postgame ingestion
queue.why: Scoring is manual, so it happens rarely, so the 300-graded-unit floor is unreachable in practice. NE@SEA play-by-play was available and went unused while SF@LA was scored from a transcription.
queue.work: Poll nflverse pbp -- reachable from this executor -- hash it, store it, and score every sealed board automatically into the prospective ledger. Re-score SF@LA from authoritative bytes when published and keep both rows.

queue.title: Score the QB room aggregate apart from the per-QB split
queue.why: NE@SEA is the cleanest evidence either game produced. The Seattle room aggregate was nearly exact -- 200 passing yards against 197.46, 24 attempts against 27.44 -- while the split was maximally wrong, Darnold forecast 24.48 attempts and throwing 2, Lock forecast 2.10 and throwing 22, because Darnold was injured early. No pregame information set could have known that.
queue.work: Report the room aggregate as a first-class estimand beside the per-QB numbers, so irreducible in-game replacement variance stops being charged to the model as allocation error.
queue.evidence_required: The reporting change needs none. Any ALLOCATION change needs >=20 games showing per-QB CRPS is improvable at all given that mid-game replacement is unobservable pregame.

queue.title: Game-state-conditioned team volume (Track 1)
queue.why: The clearest predictive signal across BOTH games. SF@LA: LA ran 57 plays against 65.65 while losing 27-7. NE@SEA: NE took 42 dropbacks against 33.69 while trailing. Model and market also missed the same direction on 6 of 8 SF@LA markets, which points at environment rather than player share.
queue.work: Pre-register a game-state conditioning design with a sealed holdout.
queue.evidence_required: >=20 prospective games, CRPS with clustering by date and team, decided out of sample. TWO GAMES CANNOT PROMOTE THIS and must not be used to tune it.

queue.title: Appearance and role certainty
queue.why: Appearance is the gate on five of nine layers, and inactive redistribution helped receivers while hurting the lead back (McCaffrey CRPS 1.48 -> 2.14).
queue.work: Study role certainty as a separate quantity from appearance probability; pre-register before changing any allocation.
queue.evidence_required: >=20 games, by position group, out of sample.

queue.title: Receiving-conversion calibration
queue.why: TWO games now show the same shape: the team that threw more than forecast gained fewer yards per attempt than forecast. NE 42 dropbacks (+8.31) but 178 yards (-34.46); Purdy 34 attempts vs 26.71 but 205 yards vs 210.50. Offsetting errors make yardage look accurate while both components are wrong.
queue.work: Decompose yards into volume x efficiency and score the parts separately.
queue.evidence_required: >=300 graded metrics for any calibration claim, per this project own floors. Sixteen correlated metrics from one game support nothing.

queue.title: Incomplete-layer visibility
queue.why: "12 complete / 0 blocked" described twelve QB-only boards as complete.
queue.work: Shipped: EXECUTION_STATE and FORECAST_COMPLETENESS are independent, the nine-layer matrix is computed from stored distributions, and ranking eligibility is per market causal path.

queue.title: Pregame data capture resilience
queue.why: The content_markers defect hid behind an egress block for days, and the executor that could fetch found it inside the one window that mattered.
queue.work: Assert that a capture whose parse yields an empty-state page cannot discharge its obligation; alert on a window closing unfilled rather than recording it silently.

queue.title: Operational latency: warm session
queue.why: A fresh process pays ~65s before the first forecast, so a one-game refresh costs 81s instead of ~11s.
queue.work: Diagnosis complete: slate_fits 53.9s, enriched_frame 51.1s within it. A warm-session mode reusing immutable, content-hash-keyed state across refreshes is designed but NOT BUILT.
queue.evidence_required: Benchmarks A-D, with C near the 10.7s marginal cost.

queue.title: Remaining intentionally unmodeled markets
queue.why: RB/WR/TE rushing yards remain unavailable pending RUSHING_CONVERSION_CONTROL_UNDEFINED, and no aging curve or handedness split exists anywhere.
queue.work: Leave unmodeled. They are declared absences, not defects, and the board marks them NOT_MODELED rather than guessing.
queue.evidence_required: A resolution of the rushing conversion control comes first; carries x YPC is explicitly forbidden.

correction_note: CORRECTED 2026-09-11. The previous version was built on the false premise that NE@SEA had never been forecast. It had. Both games are prospective case studies and the queue is rebuilt on n=2.
